title: One Divine, Many Forms
objective: After this level you can explain how many Hindus worship Vishnu, Shiva or the Goddess as forms of one ultimate reality.
summary: Most Hindus believe in one Supreme God whose forms are many deities. Each person may choose a form to love, and three great traditions center on Vishnu, Shiva and Devi.

cards.headline: Two neighbors pray at two different shrines, one to Shiva, one to Vishnu.
cards.body: Are they worshipping different gods? Many Hindus would say they are approaching the same Supreme God through different forms. Here's how one and many fit together.

cards.headline: One light, many lamps
cards.body: Outsiders often call Hindus polytheists, yet many Hindus describe themselves as monotheists. Both labels reach for something real. Most Hindus believe in one Supreme God whose qualities and forms are shown in many deities. Many believe all the deities are aspects of one transcendent power, and some see particular deities as forms of Brahman, the power you met in Level 42. Picture a row of lamps lit from a single flame.

cards.headline: Your chosen form
cards.body: Which form do you pray to? Hindu tradition leaves room to choose. Each person can relate to God through a chosen form, the ishta devata, "desired form of God". One person is drawn to Shiva, another to Krishna, another to the goddess Kali. It's a bit like many doors into the same house: you use the one that feels like yours.

cards.headline: Three great traditions
cards.body: Devotion gathered into great traditions that took shape in the Gupta period, 320 to 500 CE. Vaishnavism centers on Vishnu and his avatars, such as Rama and Krishna. Shaivism centers on Shiva. Shaktism centers on Devi, the Goddess. A classic trio, the Trimurti, sums up the divine work: Brahma creates, Vishnu preserves, and Shiva destroys in order to re-create.

cards.headline: One Divine, Many Forms: the takeaways
learned: Most Hindus see one Supreme God in many forms
Each person may choose a form: the ishta devata
Vaishnavism, Shaivism and Shaktism center on Vishnu, Shiva and Devi

questions.prompt: Which Hindu tradition centers on Devi, the Goddess?

options.label: Vedanta
options.rationale: That's a name for the Upanishads.

questions.explanation: Shaktism centers on Devi, the Goddess; Vaishnavism on Vishnu; Shaivism on Shiva.

questions.prompt: Why can two Hindus devoted to different deities see themselves as worshipping one reality?

options.label: Each region of India allows just one deity
options.rationale: People choose their own form of God.

options.label: Many Hindus see all deities as aspects of one transcendent power
Both deities are secretly the same Goddess
options.rationale: The belief is about one Supreme God in many forms.

options.label: The Vedas name only a single god
options.rationale: The Vedic hymns praise many gods.

questions.explanation: Most Hindus believe in one Supreme God shown in many deities, and each person may choose a form (ishta devata).

questions.prompt: Level 42 described Brahman as the power upholding everything. How do some Hindus link Brahman to the many deities?

options.label: Brahman is one rival deity among many
options.rationale: Brahman upholds everything; it isn't a rival.

options.label: The deities replaced Brahman in later times
options.rationale: Many see the deities as its forms.

options.label: They see particular deities as forms of Brahman
Brahman is the name of the Shiva tradition

questions.explanation: Some Hindus regard particular deities as manifestations of Brahman, the one power behind all.
